scan_notes: 3CE is a Community Choice Aggregator (public JPA of Central Coast cities/counties) that sets generation rates for customers inside PG&E and SCE service territory (CAISO); PG&E/SCE own the wires, handle interconnection, and run C&I interruptible/DR programs (BIP, CBP, DRAM) that HFP participants cannot double-enroll in. 3CE co-runs residential/commercial/ag Hourly Flex Pricing (real-time hourly rate pilot w/ PG&E) and its Residential Battery Rebate Program (peak-hour discharge requirement, closed to new apps 3/2026) is being replaced by a true dispatchable VPP launching Fall 2026. ownership_type recorded as Municipal as closest fit (public agency, not a private IOU/co-op).

GS-3/GS-4/GS-5 commercial rates have built-in Off-Peak/On-Peak/Super-Peak TOU energy charges. Power Flex (EnergyHub-run smart-thermostat DR, $25 enrollment + annual credit) covers both residential customers and small commercial GS-1 (Power Flex Business).

Large commercial L-1/L-2 rates have built-in On-Peak/Off-Peak TOU energy charges. Smart Thermostat Rebate is a one-time purchase incentive only (no utility control/DR event language found) so marked No for res_dispatch. No C&I interruptible/curtailment/DSGS program found on PWP's own site.

scan_notes: Burbank (with Glendale) sits in LADWP's own balancing authority, not CAISO. Residential has an optional EV Time-of-Use rate (Summer On/Mid/Off-Peak). Cool Rewards is a bring-your-own-device smart-thermostat DR program open to both residential AND small commercial electric service (utility sends DR events that adjust the thermostat) -- counted for both res_dispatch and ci_dispatch. BWP also facilitates large C&I enrollment in the statewide DSGS program per city council documents, not yet confirmed on BWP's own program pages. Commercial rate schedules (Small/Medium/Large/XL General Service) are demand-charge based per the Adopted Fee Schedule Article X; no clear TOU/shifting-oriented commercial rate design found in the portions reviewed.

IOU, CPUC-regulated (tariffs filed as CPUC Advice Letters, unlike the municipal/irrigation-district targets in this cluster). Serves the South Lake Tahoe / Lake Tahoe basin area and sits in the NV Energy (Sierra Pacific Power) balancing authority area, not CAISO -- CalPeco procures nearly all its energy from NV Energy and has only limited CAISO ties. Optional residential Schedule TOU D-1 confirmed via own CPUC tariff sheet (capped enrollment, 1,500 meters cumulative with TOU A-1). Commercial Schedule A-1 (<20kW demand) tariff reviewed shows flat/demand-tiered structure, not clearly TOU; larger C&I schedules and any DR/interruptible or smart-thermostat dispatch program were not confirmed on Liberty's own site within search budget.

REU is a member of BANC (Balancing Authority of Northern California), not CAISO. Residential Electrification Rebates page lists only appliance/efficiency rebates (heat pump, smart-thermostat-controlled HVAC in new construction), no utility-dispatched DR/device-control program found. REU's own PDF/CMS pages did not render text for direct in-tool verification; facts corroborated via search-engine text extracts of the same own-domain pages, hence Secondary tier.

Optional EV TOU rate (Schedule D1/D2 customers with EV, smart meter required) confirmed on AMP's own site. Commercial schedules A-1/A-2/A-3 are flat energy + demand-metered (kW peak) charges, not TOU/shifting-oriented rate designs. Smart Thermostat program on the Rebates & Incentives page is a purchase rebate (D1H rate schedule, 2 per address/year), no utility dispatch/DR-event language found. No commercial curtailable/interruptible DR program found on AMP's own site.
